history.heading: Lucayans and Columbus
paragraphs: The Bahamas, an archipelago of about 700 islands and thousands of cays, were inhabited by the Lucayans, a Taíno people. Christopher Columbus made his first landfall in the Americas in the Bahamas in October 1492, probably on San Salvador.
Within a few decades the Spanish had enslaved and removed the Lucayan population, leaving the islands largely empty.

history.heading: Pirates, Loyalists and colonial rule
paragraphs: English Puritans from Bermuda settled Eleuthera in 1648. In the early 18th century Nassau became a notorious haven for pirates, including Blackbeard, until Britain restored order in 1718.

After the American Revolution, Loyalists brought enslaved Africans and tried to establish cotton plantations, which failed on the thin soils. Slavery was abolished in 1834. The islands later prospered from blockade running during the American Civil War and rum running during Prohibition.

history.heading: Independence
paragraphs: The Progressive Liberal Party, led by Lynden Pindling, won majority rule in 1967, ending the dominance of a white merchant elite known as the Bay Street Boys. The Bahamas became independent on 10 July 1973.
Hurricane Dorian in 2019 caused catastrophic damage in Abaco and Grand Bahama.

culture.heading: Junkanoo and island traditions
paragraphs: Bahamian culture blends African, British and American influences. Junkanoo, a street parade with goatskin drums, cowbells, whistles and elaborate costumes, takes place on Boxing Day and New Year's Day.

English is the official language, and Bahamian Creole is widely spoken. Christianity, especially Baptist, Anglican and Catholic, is central to community life. Conch is the signature food, served as fritters, salad or stew, along with peas and rice.

politics.heading: Parliamentary democracy
paragraphs: The Bahamas is a parliamentary democracy and a Commonwealth realm with the British monarch as head of state, represented by a governor-general. The prime minister leads the government, and the elected House of Assembly and appointed Senate form Parliament.
Politics is dominated by two parties, the Progressive Liberal Party and the Free National Movement.

economy.heading: Tourism and finance
paragraphs: The Bahamas is one of the wealthiest countries in the Caribbean. Tourism, including resorts and cruise ships, provides most jobs and income, and international financial services are the second pillar.

There is no personal income tax; government revenue comes mainly from customs duties and value-added tax. The Bahamian dollar is pegged one-to-one to the US dollar. The country is highly vulnerable to hurricanes and rising sea levels, as most land lies just a few metres above sea level.
